faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about ABA therapy, Regional Centers, and finding resources in Los Angeles County
faq.aba1A:
Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is a scientific, evidence-based therapy that helps improve specific behaviors, such as social skills, communication, reading, and academics, as well as adaptive learning skills.

ABA therapy is particularly effective for individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and developmental disabilities. It uses positive reinforcement and data-driven techniques to teach new skills and reduce challenging behaviors.
faq.aba2Q: Who can benefit from ABA therapy?
faq.aba2A:
ABA therapy can benefit individuals of all ages with:

  • Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) - Most common use case
  • Developmental Disabilities - Cognitive or intellectual delays
  • Learning Disabilities - Academic challenges
  • Behavioral Disorders - ADHD, ODD, and others
  • Communication Disorders - Speech and language delays

While ABA is most commonly used for children with autism, it can be beneficial for anyone needing structured behavioral intervention.
faq.aba3Q: How long does ABA therapy take?
faq.aba3A:
ABA therapy duration varies based on individual needs:

  • Intensive programs: 20-40 hours per week (common for young children with autism)
  • Focused programs: 10-20 hours per week (specific skill development)
  • Consultation: 1-5 hours per week (maintenance or specific issues)

Timeline: Most children participate for 1-3 years, but some may need longer or shorter periods depending on their progress and goals.
faq.rc1A:
Regional Centers are nonprofit agencies funded by the State of California that provide services and support to individuals with developmental disabilities.

They serve as the main point of contact for accessing state-funded services including ABA therapy, respite care, day programs, and more.
faq.rc2Q: How do I find my Regional Center?
faq.rc2A:
Your Regional Center is determined by your ZIP code. Use our Regional Centers page or enter your ZIP code in the map to find which one serves your area.

Los Angeles County is served by 7 Regional Centers, each covering specific geographic areas.
faq.rc3A: Yes! Services through Regional Centers are free for eligible individuals with developmental disabilities. Eligibility is based on having a qualifying developmental disability that began before age 18.
faq.ins1A:
Many insurance plans cover ABA therapy, especially for autism. Coverage varies by plan:

  • Private Insurance: California law requires coverage for autism treatment
  • Medi-Cal: Covers ABA therapy for eligible individuals
  • Regional Centers: May fund services not covered by insurance
faq.ins2Q: What if I don't have insurance?
faq.ins2A:
If you don't have insurance, you still have options:

  • Apply for Medi-Cal (California's Medicaid program)
  • Contact your Regional Center for state-funded services
  • Ask resources about sliding scale fees
  • Check for grant programs and scholarships
faq.map1Q: How do I use the KINDD map?
faq.map1A:
Using the map is easy:

  1. Enter your ZIP code or allow location access
  2. Browse resources in your area
  3. Use filters to narrow by therapy type, insurance, etc.
  4. Click on a resource for details and contact info
faq.map2A: Our resources are verified through Regional Center vendor lists and direct outreach. We update information regularly, but always recommend calling to confirm details before your first visit.

intro.title: Welcome to the KiNDD Resource Navigator
intro.lead: This application is designed to help families find developmental services and therapies for their children throughout Los Angeles County.

howItWorks.title: How does it work?
howItWorks.body: You will be asked a few questions about your child's needs, age, and location to help identify relevant services and resources in your area.

services.title: What services can I find?
services.body: The Resource Navigator can help you explore services such as Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), occupational therapy (OT), physical therapy (PT), speech-language therapy (SLP), and other developmental services.

audience.title: Who can use this application?
audience.body: This tool is intended to support families, caregivers, and clinicians of children with neurodevelopmental disabilities or developmental concerns who are looking for services and support.

afterQuestions.title: What happens after I answer the questions?
afterQuestions.body: Based on your responses, the application will help you identify potentially relevant providers and services. You can use this information to explore your options and contact providers directly to learn more about their services, availability, and eligibility requirements.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.body: Your answers to these questions are saved on your device so KiNDD can remember your preferences. Your ZIP code or location is sent to KiNDD only to find services near you, and we don't keep a history of your searches tied to you. KiNDD doesn't require an account, and we don't sell your information. If you use Ask KiNDD, your question and these answers are sent to help answer it. See our {privacyLink} for details.

language.title: Language and accessibility
language.body: KiNDD is available in English and Spanish. You can change the language at any time from the language menu (English / Español). If you need help using KiNDD, email {email}.

keepInMind.title: Please keep in mind
keepInMind.body: The KiNDD Resource Navigator is an informational tool, not a substitute for medical consultation or professional advice. It does not provide diagnoses or official medical recommendations. Please consult a licensed healthcare provider when making decisions about your child's care.

providers.title: About service providers
providers.body: The KiNDD team works to maintain an accurate and useful directory of developmental service providers. However, services, availability, eligibility requirements, and provider information may change. Inclusion in the application does not constitute an endorsement or guarantee of a provider's services or quality of care.

urgent.title: Urgent concerns
urgent.body: The KiNDD Resource Navigator is not intended for emergencies or urgent medical concerns. If your child is experiencing a medical emergency, please call 911 or go to your nearest hospital's Emergency Department.

help.title: We're here to help
help.body: Finding developmental services can feel overwhelming, and we hope this tool makes it easier to explore your options and connect with resources that support your child and family. Please contact {email} with any questions or concerns.
